claims.text: Minor boron doping enhances boundary cohesion in eutectic high-entropy alloys with lamellar colonies.
Minor boron doping increases room-temperature tensile strength relative to an undoped lamellar-colony alloy.
Minor boron doping increases room-temperature tensile ductility relative to an undoped lamellar-colony alloy.
The proposed boron addition is approximately 0.1–0.5 at.%.
Homogenization and aging after boron addition will promote uniform boron dissolution and controlled boundary segregation.
Standard solution treatment and aging can retain well-defined lamellar colonies while permitting controlled boron segregation.
Excessively high boron content can cause coarse boride formation.
Added boron segregates at lamellar interfaces and grain boundaries.
Boron-induced boundary cohesion suppresses microcrack initiation at colony boundaries during tensile loading.
Suppression of colony-boundary microcracking produces both higher yield strength and greater ambient-temperature ductility.
Boron doping will increase yield strength by approximately 10–20% relative to the undoped baseline.
Boron doping will increase room-temperature tensile ductility by approximately 5–10 percentage points relative to the undoped baseline.
The beneficial effect requires boron content below the solubility limit and avoidance of extensive boride precipitation.
Large brittle borides formed at excessive boron content could eliminate the strengthening and ductilizing benefit.
The optimal boron concentration may vary with the eutectic high-entropy alloy composition.
Excessive boron may generate secondary phases that reintroduce brittleness.
